items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-04-07
items.q: Now that's why we just used this fellow they called Walter Decon when I was the last one.

ctx.x: No, John Handy played saxophone and clarinet. Yeah, that's right. And the bass player, Sylvester.

But he played a while there with us. And also Duke Deconje played the piano. And Butler rap. Gaillet. Gaillet, yeah. He played the guitar. And I played the drum. Duke Deconje? Duke Deconje, yeah. He played the piano with us. Does he play any other instruments? No, he just played none of the piano. He got killed. You know he had a shoe shop there on Ramport near Common and he went out with this this fellow played the piano, Richardson they called him. Herbert Richardson, you know Herbert Richardson? No? Well he…
He must have had a different guitar player too after that. Yeah we did.

items.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15
items.q: I played there with a fella that's called Rap. I don't know if you've already talked about him. Played guitar. Rap, yeah, that's right. And young, you call him Spook. And handy, played the bass. And Decaugé

ctx.x: I know where you, on Ivyville. Yeah, that's right. I played there five years. I played from, oh, I retired. I played from 35 up to 42. 35 up to 42 I played there with a fella that's called Rap. I don't know if you've already talked about him. Played guitar. Rap, yeah, that's right. And young, you call him Spook. And handy, played the bass. And Decaugé, you might have heard him talk about him. I would have been playing the write-up about him. Decaugé. No, I don't think I know.
No? That was a wonderful piano player.
